subject.title: Telegram: per-chat lane serialization (isolated ingress) starves messages.queue.collect — same-chat bursts never coalesce

question: Should busy same-lane Telegram spooled updates be admitted into the active follow-up/collect queue, or should Telegram document `collect` as unsupported for same-chat isolated-ingress bursts?
rationale: The bug is source-supported, but the repair crosses Telegram durable spool semantics and core active-run queue ownership, so automation should not choose the permanent delivery contract alone.

options.title: Bridge busy-lane updates into collect
options.body: Implement a Telegram-aware admission path that preserves durable-before-ack, replay, lane ordering, and control-lane escapes while letting same-chat bursts join the active queue.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep strict per-chat lane serialization and make Telegram same-chat `collect` limitations explicit in config/channel docs.

options.title: Defer to shared queue design
options.body: Keep this as the canonical design item until maintainers decide a cross-channel ingress/dispatcher contract instead of a Telegram-only bridge.

recommendation.title: Bridge busy-lane updates into collect
recommendation.body: Implement a Telegram-aware admission path that preserves durable-before-ack, replay, lane ordering, and control-lane escapes while letting same-chat bursts join the active queue.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the adjacent follow-up ordering and active-run steering work and are the strongest available routing signal for the product boundary choice.
